Synthetic difference in differences

Source: R/sdidx.R
sdidx.Rd

The estimator of Arkhangelsky et al. (2021) for units adopting a policy in one period: comparison units weighted so that their path before adoption parallels the treated units', periods before adoption weighted so that they predict the comparison units' level after, and the difference in differences taken with both weights.

Usage

sdidx(y, unit, time, first, reps = 200, seed = NULL, level = 0.95)

Arguments

y

The outcome: finite numbers, one per row (counts from 0 for fam = "pois" or "nb").

unit

The unit of each row: labels.

time

The period of each row: numbers; a balanced panel.

first

The period each row's unit is first treated, one period for every treated unit; NA, 0 or Inf for the comparison units.

reps

The placebo draws: a whole number, at least 2.

seed

The seed of the placebo draws: NULL to draw it from R's generator, or a whole number from 0.

level

The confidence level of the normal interval.

Value

An object of class sdidx, a list: est (est, se, lo, hi); meth ("placebo" or "jackknife"); unitw (unit, w); timew (time, w); path (time, treated, the treated mean, and synth, the weighted comparison units); level.

Details

With N0 comparison units, N1 treated, T0 periods before adoption and T1 after, the unit weights solve min (1/T0) sum_{t <= T0} (w0 + sum_j w_j y_jt - ybar_1t)^2 + zeta^2 ||w||^2 over the simplex, with zeta = (N1 T1)^(1/4) sigma and sigma the standard deviation of the comparison units' first differences before adoption; the time weights solve the same problem across comparison units, predicting each unit's mean after adoption from its periods before, with zeta = 1e-6 sigma. The estimate is (ybar_1,post - sum_t l_t ybar_1t) - sum_j w_j (ybar_j,post - sum_t l_t y_jt). The weights are the exact solutions of these convex problems (Wolfe's minimum-norm point); the 'synthdid' package runs Frank-Wolfe steps and then sparsifies, so its estimate differs slightly. The standard error is the placebo one when one unit is treated (a comparison unit drawn at random treated as if adopting, the weights solved again, reps times; sqrt((reps - 1) / reps) times the standard deviation), and otherwise the jackknife over units with the weights held (Arkhangelsky et al. 2021, algorithms 3 and 4; NA when one comparison unit carries all the weight).

References

Arkhangelsky, D., Athey, S., Hirshberg, D. A., Imbens, G. W. and Wager, S. (2021). Synthetic difference-in-differences. American Economic Review, 111(12), 4088-4118. doi:10.1257/aer.20190159

Examples

d <- expand.grid(year = 2010:2024, town = LETTERS[1:10])
i <- match(d$town, LETTERS)
d$first <- ifelse(i <= 3, 2019, NA)
d$rate <- 20 + i + (d$year - 2010) * (0.2 + i / 20) +
  sin(seq_len(150)) - 3 * (i <= 3 & d$year >= 2019)
sdidx(d$rate, d$town, d$year, d$first)
#> sdidx: standard error by jackknife
#>        est        se        lo        hi
#>  -4.019258 0.2406598 -4.490942 -3.547573
